instruction: Open the 2022 book reading spreadsheet on the desktop. Find a book that received the highest rating. Copy its title to the 'book_list_result.docx' file on the desktop.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 's'); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.explanation: Task requires finding a book with the highest rating from the spreadsheet. Verified with Python: Four books have rating 5.0 (Fire and Blood, Song of Solomon, The Andromeda Strain, Silence). Accepting Fire and Blood as the first one in the list. The evaluator checks if the DOCX file contains 'Fire and Blood'.

llm_judge_reasons: The metric function correctly handles the expected parameter. When expected.type='rule', the framework returns {'text': 'Fire and Blood'}, and the metric properly extracts the text using 'expected.get('text', '')' at lines 16-19.
The getter logic correctly extracts text content from the DOCX file using python-docx library, reading all paragraphs and joining them.
The metric logic correctly performs case-insensitive, whitespace-normalized substring matching to check if 'Fire and Blood' appears in the document.
Postconfig appropriately activates the Writer window and saves the file (Ctrl+S) to ensure fresh file content is read.

Minor semantic issue: The instruction says 'Find a book that received the highest rating', allowing any of the 4 books with rating 5.0 (Fire and Blood, Song of Solomon, The Andromeda Strain, Silence). However, the evaluator only accepts 'Fire and Blood'. This is overly restrictive but acknowledged in metadata as an intentional choice for consistency.
The evaluator will work correctly at runtime and can verify that the user copied a highest-rated book title (specifically 'Fire and Blood') to the DOCX file.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider updating the metric to accept any of the 4 highest-rated book titles if the instruction truly allows 'a book' (any one). This could be done by changing expected.rules.text to a list: ['Fire and Blood', 'Song of Solomon', 'The Andromeda Strain', 'Silence'] and checking if any appears in the document.
Alternatively, clarify the instruction to say 'Copy the title Fire and Blood' if only one specific answer is acceptable.
